references.text: The context of the verse describing the requirement to bring sacrificial animals to the entrance of the tabernacle instead of offering them elsewhere.
Instructions regarding peace offerings (זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים) that are to be brought to the Lord at the entrance of the tent.
Command to bring sacrifices to the place the Lord chooses, not just anywhere.
Warning against offering burnt offerings anywhere; only at the chosen place.
Instruction to build an altar and offer burnt offerings and peace offerings at the place the Lord designates.
Burnt offerings are to be brought to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before the presence of the Lord.
Reference to Israel's idolatry by offering on open fields and hills, in violation of the Lord's command.
The people continued to offer at the high places, even though it was to the Lord—this shows the need for centralized worship.
Jesus as the perfect sacrifice brought outside the camp, fulfilling the sacrificial laws given to the priests.
